cells.verb: tending what grows with steady, responsible care
cells.place: in the place where you let things go on purpose
cells.ask: Let one person see what it cost you to put that down — not so they'll lift it, just so it's witnessed. What comes back is a letting-go that feels like finishing, not losing.
cells.core:
You're taking as much care with what's leaving as with what's staying. The thing you're setting down gets tended right up to the door — fed, sorted, handed off properly — and the thing you're keeping gets the room it needed. Neither one is being rushed. That's rarer than it sounds: most people either cling or drop. You're doing the slow middle thing, and it's working.

There's one piece still in your hands that doesn't have to be. Nobody has seen what this clearing asked of you. Letting one person see it won't change the release — it will finish it.
cells.sheetLine: You tend what you're letting go of as carefully as what you keep.

cells.tense: Future — bracing at a future you can't write in yet.
cells.verb: tending what grows, now past the point where it needs you
cells.place: in the place where you let things go on purpose
cells.ask: Name one thing that already came of your tending — something that grew, finished, is real — and sit with it as done. What comes back is care that doesn't wear you out, and hands that can hold something without closing.
cells.core:
You're still minding what you've already decided to release. Somewhere ahead is a version where it doesn't go well without you, and you're living there — checking, adjusting, making sure the handoff is perfect — so the letting-go never actually happens. It just becomes another thing you manage.

The care isn't the problem. It's pointed at a future that hasn't arrived and may not. What it hasn't been pointed at is what the tending already produced.
cells.sheetLine: You're still tending the thing you said you'd let go.

cells.tense: Past — still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: tending what grows, with hands that have stopped reaching
cells.place: in the place where you let things go on purpose
cells.ask: Pick one thing you still want to see grow and give it real attention this week, knowing it may not stay. What comes back is care that doesn't exhaust you, because it stopped being a bargain against loss.
cells.core:
You've stopped tending because things leave anyway. Somewhere back there, something you cared for went out the door regardless, and the lesson you took was: why water what you'll lose. So the letting-go has quietly turned into not-bothering. Things aren't being released now; they're being left.

The care didn't disappear. It just stopped going anywhere. And a clearing nobody tends isn't space — it's just empty.
cells.sheetLine: Letting go turned into not bothering.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: tending what grows, and deciding what doesn't
cells.place: in the place where you let things go on purpose
cells.ask: Say to one person, plainly, "I chose to let that go" — one thing you've been describing as just falling away. What comes back is a release that feels like something you finished, not something that happened to you.
cells.core:
You're already choosing what goes and taking real care with how it goes — what gets handed off, what gets kept, what gets quietly retired. People around you can see the hand in it. But you describe it as things just thinning out, running their course, nothing you did.

The tending is deliberate. The choosing is yours. It's only the saying-so that's missing — and without it, nobody can see what the choosing asked of you, including you.
cells.sheetLine: You're choosing what goes. You call it things falling away.
